rules.statement: Code that signs through a remote key management service (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS and similar) must handle HTTP 429 throttling responses with back-off instead of failing the operation outright.
rules.why: Remote vaults throttle per vault, and the signer sits on the token path, so a throttled call has to back off rather than fail the token request.
rules.check: Look at new or changed remote-signer or key-wrapper adapters for handling of 429/throttling errors with a retry and back-off. Report a signer that surfaces the first 429 as a failure.

rules.statement: Serve JWKS from cached public keys rather than calling the remote key management service each time the key set is requested.
rules.why: Each remote call adds a network round-trip and costs money, and public keys can safely be cached.
rules.check: Look for JWKS or public-key endpoints that call the KMS or vault client on every request and have no cache.

rules.statement: When a forwarded client-certificate header is present but its value can't be decoded, fail the request with `invalid_request` instead of treating it as if no certificate was presented.
rules.why: Reading a malformed forwarded certificate as absent hides errors and can quietly change which authentication path the request takes.
rules.check: In the code that parses forwarded certificate headers (for example Traefik's `X-Forwarded-Tls-Client-Cert`), look for decode failures that return null or no certificate instead of an `invalid_request` error.

rules.statement: Read a forwarded client-certificate header that holds a comma-separated chain with the client's own certificate first, and pass the remaining certificates on as intermediates for chain building.
rules.why: The proxy forwards the whole chain, comma-separated with the leaf first, and the server needs the intermediates to validate the leaf against its trust anchors.
rules.check: Look at how forwarded-certificate parsing handles a value containing commas. Report code that decodes only the whole value, picks the wrong certificate as the leaf, or drops the intermediates.

rules.statement: For `tls_client_auth` (RFC 8705), build the presented certificate's chain to the configured trust anchors (with the `clientAuth` EKU, validity period and the configured revocation mode) before matching the subject, and trust no certificate when no anchor is configured.
rules.why: The server, not the proxy, enforces each tenant's and client's PKI trust. Without anchors, no chain can be trusted, so the check must fail closed.
rules.check: In mTLS client-authentication code, look for subject matching done without validating the chain first, for chain building that falls back to the system root store, for a missing EKU or validity check, or for code that accepts a certificate when the trust-anchor list is empty.

rules.statement: When the shared store behind replay-protection checks (DPoP nonces, single-use proof and client-assertion `jti`s) can't be reached, fail those checks closed and report the instance as not ready on its health check.
rules.why: Accepting proofs or assertions without the shared replay record would let a replay through across replicas.
rules.check: Look at how the shared-state adapter handles connection errors in replay, nonce or `jti` checks. Report code that treats an unreachable store as 'not seen before', or that leaves the health check reporting ready.
